"BELLINGHAM: THE UNDERGROUND — 18+ FIRST-PERSON OPEN-WORLD SIMULATOR

Create a fully playable FIRST-PERSON 3D open-world life simulator and arcade fighting game set in a fictionalized Bellingham, Washington. Rated 18+ for mature themes, adult relationships, violence, crime, drugs, alcohol, strong language, dark humor, and psychological horror. Use original characters, businesses, artwork, music, and dialogue.
OPEN WORLD: Build a detailed, explorable Bellingham inspired by Downtown, Fairhaven, Boulevard Park, the waterfront, WWU surroundings, Whatcom Falls, Lake Whatcom, Chuckanut forests, residential neighborhoods, industrial districts, beaches, marinas, and hiking trails. Include Mount Baker in the distance, realistic Pacific Northwest rain, fog, cloudy skies, wet roads, evergreen forests, wildlife, traffic, and changing weather. Use fictionalized buildings and businesses.
LIFE SIMULATION: Start as an ordinary adult living in Bellingham. Allow players to walk, drive, work, earn money, rent or buy homes, shop, cook, eat, sleep, visit restaurants, bars, coffee shops, gyms and nightclubs, date NPCs, build friendships and relationships, customize clothing, hairstyles and tattoos, own vehicles, and explore freely. Include money, inventory, housing, jobs, transportation, reputation, personal needs, and character progression.
18+ MATURE CONTENT: Include adult dating, flirting, consensual hookups, romance, intimacy, jealousy, breakups, adult nightlife, fictional strip clubs, optional non-graphic sexual encounters, and relationship consequences. Include alcohol, intoxicated NPCs, fictional drug markets, addiction storylines, overdoses, crime, theft, robbery, gambling, criminal organizations, police encounters, profanity, dark humor, blood, injuries, knockouts, and brutal arcade-style combat. All sexual characters must be adults (18+). Sexual encounters must be consensual and non-graphic; no sexual violence or exploitation.
FIRST-PERSON COMBAT: Create responsive arcade-style fighting with punches, kicks, blocks, dodges, counters, grapples, combos, special attacks, environmental attacks, stamina, health, special meters, slow-motion finishers, and different fighting styles. Every NPC could secretly be a fighter.
THE SECRET: Begin with 90% normal life and 10% strange events. The player gradually discovers Bellingham is secretly home to an enormous underground fighting tournament. Nobody explains it. A barista suddenly says \"ROUND ONE.\" A pedestrian says \"You're late.\" A bus takes the player to a hidden arena. People disappear. After fights, everyone acts normal. Gradually increase the weirdness.
FIGHTERS AND BOSSES: Create original characters including THE BARISTA (super-fast fighter), THE FERRYMAN (water-based combat), THE HIKER (nature attacks), THE MECHANIC (improvised weapons), THE STUDENT (advanced martial arts), THE OLD MAN AT THE PARK (secretly incredibly powerful), THE RAINCOAT (appears during storms), THE MAYOR (speech-based attacks), THE MIRROR (copies player abilities), and THE FUTURE PLAYER (knows the player's history). Give each unique personalities, dialogue, abilities, backstories, and quests.
RANDOM EVENTS: Include hundreds of unpredictable encounters: frozen pedestrians, whispering alleys, mysterious followers, secret dojos, gas-station challenges, strange buses, birds flying in perfect circles, coffee shops turning into arenas, and storms that change reality. Events should respond to player actions and progress.
NPC INTELLIGENCE: NPCs remember conversations, fights, relationships, and decisions. They develop friendships, rivalries, romantic relationships, and grudges. Some lie, manipulate, help, or challenge the player. Give them daily schedules, routines, and changing reactions based on reputation.
QUESTS AND PROGRESSION: Include main missions, side quests, jobs, hidden challenges, secret organizations, training locations, artifacts, alternate realities, boss battles, skills, upgrades, and reputation rankings. Allow play
"

QUESTS AND PROGRESSION: Includye main missions, side quests, jobs, hidden challenges, secret organizations, training locations, artifacts, alternate realities, boss battles, skills, upgrades, and reputation rankings. Allow players to ignore the tournament and live an ordinary life indefinitely.
THE SIMULATION REVEAL: Gradually transform Bellingham into a surreal world where buildings move, roads change, NPCs repeat conversations, the ocean appears downtown, and alternate versions of the city become accessible. Reveal that the entire world is an experimental simulation designed to identify the strongest human fighter.
FINAL BATTLE AND ENDINGS: Fight the person controlling the simulation while Bellingham collapses around the player. Offer five endings: escape the simulation, become champion, shut it down, take control, or stay in Bellingham and pretend nothing happened. Make endings depend on player choices, relationships, reputation, and completed quests.
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Implement playable first-person movement, jumping, sprinting, crouching, interaction, combat, driving, NPC dialogue, inventory, money, health, stamina, saving/loading, day/night cycles, dynamic weather, traffic, pedestrians, businesses, quests, random events, and boss battles. Include keyboard/mouse and mobile touchscreen controls when supported. Use realistic lighting, detailed environments, animations, sound effects, original music, and cinematic battles.
BUILD PRIORITIES: 1. First-person movement and camera. 2. Functional combat. 3. Detailed Bellingham environment. 4. NPC interaction. 5. Life simulation. 6. Random events and quests. 7. Underground tournament. 8. Bosses and multiple endings.
IMPORTANT: Build an actual playable game, not just a visual demo. Prioritize working mechanics over empty scenery. The player must initially believe they are living an ordinary life in Bellingham. Let them discover the increasingly bizarre underground fighting conspiracy naturally. Make the experience immersive, funny, unpredictable, mature, mysterious, and completely original.

## Objective
- Build a fully playable, original 18+ first-person open-world Bellingham life simulator and arcade fighting game with an underground tournament, simulation reveal, bosses, random events, and five endings.

## Requirements
- First-person movement, jumping, sprinting, crouching, interaction, combat, driving, NPC dialogue, inventory, money, health, stamina, saving/loading, day/night, weather, traffic, pedestrians, businesses, quests, random events, bosses.
- Detailed fictionalized Bellingham: Downtown, Fairhaven, Boulevard Park, waterfront, WWU, Whatcom Falls, Lake Whatcom, Chuckanut, residential/industrial areas, marina, trails, Mount Baker, rain/fog/wet roads/forests/wildlife/traffic.
- Life sim: walk/drive/work/earn, rent/buy homes, shop/cook/eat/sleep, restaurants/bars/cafes/gyms/clubs, date/relationships, clothing/hair/tattoos, vehicles, reputation, needs, progression.
- Mature content must remain consensual, adult-only, non-graphic; sexual encounters fade to black. No sexual violence/exploitation.
- Combat: punches/kicks/blocks/dodges/counters/grapples/combos/specials/environmental attacks/stamina/health/special meters/slow-mo finishers/styles.
- Story starts 90% normal and gradually reveals an underground tournament and simulation. Weirdness grows through events, bosses, and chapters.
- Ten bosses required: THE BARISTA, THE FERRYMAN, THE HIKER, THE MECHANIC, THE STUDENT, THE OLD MAN AT THE PARK, THE RAINCOAT, THE MAYOR, THE MIRROR, THE FUTURE PLAYER.
- Include hundreds of generated random encounters, NPC memory/schedules/relationships/grudges, quests, jobs, artifacts, secret organizations, alternate realities, training, skills, reputation ranks.
- Allow ignoring the tournament and living normally indefinitely.
- Final controller battle and five endings: escape, champion, shut down, take control, stay.
- Keyboard/mouse and mobile touchscreen controls.
- Must be an actual playable game, not a visual demo; working mechanics prioritized.
- Original characters, businesses, art, music, dialogue.

## Decisions
- Building a static HTML/CSS/JS Three.js app with local vendored Three.js and local fonts, no framework/build step.
- Procedural low-poly 3D world, canvas-generated textures/signage, Web Audio procedural music/SFX.
- Split implementation into modular ES modules under `src/`.
- Persistence via `localStorage` key `bellingham_underground_save_v3`.
- 18+ consent gate in menu; all romance/intimacy explicitly adult, consensual, non-graphic.
- Arena located at `(420,-300)` as hidden Terminal 9 zone; city Terminal 9 entrance at `(184,-206)`.
- Story stage model: 0 normal, 1 round one, 2 undercurrent, 3 seven names, 4 storm/raincoat, 5 mirror, 6 future, 7 endings.
- Boss roster unlocks progressively; three challenger wins after Barista trigger simulation reveal/storm.
- Alternate reality via a dynamic “thin door” at the phone booth after truth reveal.
- Five endings gated by artifacts, boss completion, reputation, Quiet Table alliance, relationships.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full project skeleton: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/` modules.
- Installed/copied Three.js `vendor/three.module.js` and `three.core.js`; copied fonts into `fonts/`.
- Implemented `src/data.js`: districts, businesses, items, 18 NPCs, 10 bosses, quests, side quests, endings, events, styles, weather, ranks, customization options.
- Implemented `src/world.js`: sky shader, lighting/fog, terrain, water, Mount Baker, roads, wet puddles, landmark buildings, procedural buildings, signs, trees, street furniture, traffic, cars, waterfront, arena, ghost city/ocean/fragments, rain/fog/wildlife, collisions, interactables, weather/weirdness.
- Implemented `src/npcs.js`: procedural human models, named/ambient NPCs, boss accessories, schedules, walking/idle animation, name labels, freezing/following, nearest NPC.
- Implemented `src/player.js`: first-person movement, collision, sprint/crouch/jump, stamina, head bob, arms/punch/kick/block animations, driving/chase camera, teleport.
- Implemented `src/audio.js`: procedural rain/hum/pads, footsteps, impacts, thunder, car, fight beat, UI/voice blips.
- Implemented `src/combat.js`: fight start/end, punch/kick/grapple/environment attacks, block/counter/dodge logic partially, boss AI, boss specials, combo/special meters, slow-mo finisher, impact particles/rings.
- Implemented `src/ui.js`: HUD, needs, clock/weather, minimap, full map, toasts, area/event banners, dialogue, panels, modal, combat HUD, fade/cinema, pause/settings visibility, damage numbers.
- Implemented first large portion of `src/main.js`: state/default/merge/save, boot/start/loop, simulation needs/time, weather, quest refresh, objective beacon, interactions, dialogue/romance/consent/jealousy, items, business menus, home/sleep, phone groundwork pending.
- `node --input-type=module --check < src/main.js` passes after latest append.

### Active
- Finishing `src/main.js`: transit/arena/phone/settings/input bindings, combat start/end/story progression, boss intros, random events, alternate reality, endings, touch controls, save/load UI, final integration.
- Add missing CSS for timing minigame, boss roster, journal, ending cards, phone-specific layout, damage numbers.
- Remove/avoid root `package.json` because runtime static-project detection treats package.json as unsupported package project; final deployment needs only `index.html` and assets.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Append remaining `src/main.js` sections: `startTimingGame`/`updateTiming`, `openTransit`, `hiddenBus`, `openArena`, `startArenaBoss`, `showBossIntro`, `startFight`, `handleFightEnd`, `onBossDefeated`, `openPhone`, phone tabs/actions, skill spending, style changes.
2. Add `canChallengeBoss`, `updateStoryVisibility`, `revealTruth`, `toggleAlternate`, `triggerRandomEvent`, `openEndingChoices`, `chooseEnding`, and final epilogue flow.
3. Add `bindEvents`, `setupTouch`, settings/pause/map/menu handlers, pointer lock/mouse/keyboard, resize, beforeunload save.
4. Patch `src/combat.js` to add missing `dodge()` and block/counter state handling if not already fully wired.
5. Patch `src/ui.js` modal actions to support disabled ending choices; add journal/roster/timing CSS.
6. Run app via static server, test with Playwright, fix console errors/visual issues, verify start → work shift → bus → Barista → 3 bosses → Raincoat → Mirror → Future → endings.
7. Remove root `package.json`/`node_modules` from deployment path if needed, ensure `start.sh` static HTML path works, and commit changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: main orchestrator, currently incomplete but syntax-valid; append remaining functions.
- `src/world.js`: world geometry/interactables/weather/weirdness; already substantial.
- `src/combat.js`: fight logic; needs final integration and missing dodge/block helpers.
- `src/ui.js`: all HUD/panels/dialogue/map/combat UI; modal disabled support needed.
- `src/data.js`: all content definitions and IDs used throughout.
- `src/npcs.js`: NPC models/schedules/interactions support.
- `src/player.js`: movement/driving/first-person arms.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural audio.
- `index.html`: DOM IDs expected by `ui.js` and `main.js`.
- `styles.css`: layout/visual styling; new classes still needed.
- `vendor/three.module.js`, `vendor/three.core.js`: local Three.js runtime.
- `fonts/`: local Bebas/Plex/Inter fonts.
- `start.sh`, `capture.sh`, `startup.sh`: runtime scripts.
- `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `node_modules/`: npm artifacts; likely must remove to allow static project detection.

## Important Context
- Working directory: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`.
- No commits made yet; all work is uncommitted.
- `start.sh` invokes runtime `default-start.mjs`; it detects `package.json` before `index.html` and throws “Unsupported package project” unless custom start is used. Remove root `package.json` or customize startup.
- Use `node --input-type=module --check < src/main.js` for syntax checks because root package lacks `"type":"module"`.
- `src/main.js` currently references undefined functions: `canChallengeBoss`, `startFight`, `showBossIntro`, `startTimingGame`, `updateTiming`, `openTransit`, `openArena`, `openPhone`, `bindEvents`, `setupTouch`, `updateStoryVisibility`, `toggleAlternate`, `triggerRandomEvent`, `updateEvents`, `openEndingChoices`, `chooseEnding`.
- `src/ui.js` references `ui.setStyle`, `ui.damageNumber`, `ui.flashHit`, etc.; all are implemented.
- `src/combat.js` references `audio.impact` optionally and UI methods; fine.
- Menu auto-capture clicks a button whose exact label is `START`; ensure `#btn-start` is enabled only after boot and remains the sole exact-match visible button.
- Start state should be directly in-game after clicking START, with HUD visible and objective “Clock in at The Steam Kettle.”
- Main quest stage triggers: first shift → stage 1; hidden bus → stage 2; Barista win → stage 3; 3 more boss wins → stage 4 storm; Raincoat → stage 5; Mirror → stage 6; Future → stage 7/endings.
- Boss IDs: `barista`, `ferryman`, `hiker`, `mechanic`, `student`, `oldman`, `raincoat`, `mayor`, `mirror`, `future`.
- Business IDs and entrance coordinates are in `src/data.js`; arena object is `world.arena = {x:420,z:-300}`.
- Intimacy UI must fade to black and state explicit consent; do not add explicit content.
- Touch controls must be usable with safe-area support; existing DOM IDs are `touch-stick`, `touch-look`, `touch-actions`, `touch-fight`.
- `localStorage` save/load and “CONTINUE” menu button need final verification.

## Objective
- Build a fully playable, original 18+ first-person open-world Bellingham life simulator and arcade fighting game with an underground tournament, simulation reveal, ten bosses, random events, and five endings.

## Requirements
- First-person movement, jumping, sprinting, crouching, interaction, combat, driving, NPC dialogue, inventory, money, health, stamina, saving/loading, day/night, weather, traffic, pedestrians, businesses, quests, random events, bosses.
- Detailed fictionalized Bellingham: Downtown, Fairhaven, Boulevard Park, waterfront, WWU, Whatcom Falls, Lake Whatcom, Chuckanut, residential/industrial areas, marina, trails, Mount Baker, rain/fog/wet roads/forests/wildlife/traffic.
- Life sim: walk/drive/work/earn, rent/buy homes, shop/cook/eat/sleep, restaurants/bars/cafes/gyms/clubs, date/relationships, clothing/hair/tattoos, vehicles, reputation, needs, progression.
- Mature content must remain consensual, adult-only, non-graphic; sexual encounters fade to black. No sexual violence/exploitation.
- Combat: punches/kicks/blocks/dodges/counters/grapples/combos/specials/environmental attacks/stamina/health/special meters/slow-mo finishers/styles.
- Story starts 90% normal and gradually reveals an underground tournament and simulation. Weirdness grows through events, bosses, and chapters.
- Ten bosses required: THE BARISTA, THE FERRYMAN, THE HIKER, THE MECHANIC, THE STUDENT, THE OLD MAN AT THE PARK, THE RAINCOAT, THE MAYOR, THE MIRROR, THE FUTURE PLAYER.
- Include hundreds of generated random encounters, NPC memory/schedules/relationships/grudges, quests, jobs, artifacts, secret organizations, alternate realities, training, skills, reputation ranks.
- Allow ignoring the tournament and living normally indefinitely.
- Final controller battle and five endings: escape, champion, shut down, take control, stay.
- Keyboard/mouse and mobile touchscreen controls.
- Must be an actual playable game, not a visual demo; working mechanics prioritized.
- Original characters, businesses, art, music, dialogue.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS Three.js app with local vendored Three.js and local fonts, no framework/build step.
- Procedural low-poly 3D world, canvas-generated textures/signage, Web Audio procedural music/SFX.
- Modular ES modules under `src/`.
- Persistence via `localStorage` key `bellingham_underground_save_v3`.
- 18+ consent gate in menu; romance/intimacy explicitly adult, consensual, non-graphic.
- Arena at `(420,-300)`; city Terminal 9 entrance at `(184,-206)`.
- Story stages: 0 normal, 1 round one, 2 undercurrent, 3 seven names, 4 storm/raincoat, 5 mirror, 6 future, 7 endings.
- Five endings gated by artifacts, boss completion, reputation, Quiet Table alliance, relationships.
- Removed root `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `node_modules` so runtime detects a static HTML project.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full project skeleton and all core modules implemented: `data.js`, `world.js`, `npcs.js`, `player.js`, `audio.js`, `combat.js`, `ui.js`, `main.js`.
- `src/main.js` completed with: timing minigame, transit/hidden bus, arena roster, boss progression, story reveal, alternate reality toggle, random events, phone tabs/actions, skills/styles, endings, bindings, touch controls, pause/settings/map, save/load, `boot()` invocation.
- Added debug API `window.__BELLINGHAM` exposing state/player/world/npcs/combat/ui/mode and test helpers (`openPhone`, `openArena`, `startArenaBoss`, `startTimingGame`, `timingHit`, `chooseEnding`, `openBusiness`, `setQuestStage`, `teleport`, etc.).
- `combat.js` patched with `setBlock()`, `dodge()`, and `blockTime` accumulation.
- `audio.js` patched with `impact()`.
- `ui.js` modal patched to support disabled actions.
- `styles.css` extended with timing minigame, phone layout, ending cards, locked cards, mini buttons, damage numbers, reduced motion, touch styles.
- Removed npm artifacts; static deployment path now clean.
- Fixed invalid `makeGlowTexture` color in `world.js`; brightened lighting/exposure/facades; scaled first-person arms down.
- Boot/menu/start verified via Playwright; no runtime page errors after fixes.
- Phone tabs render (status/bag/contacts/quests/style/skills/journal).

### Active
- Integration testing and bug fixing after first automated playthrough.
- Hidden bus binding fixed (transit cards use `data-act="hiddenbus"`), not yet re-verified.
- Timing minigame test did not complete after 3 clicks: mode stayed `timing`, quest stage stayed 0; needs investigation.
- Boss progression test failed because it was still stage 1 (consequence of timing/bus failures), so all later fights were locked.
- Visual quality review: initial screenshot showed very dark scene and oversized arms; lighting/arm fixes applied but not re-screenshotted.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Re-run `/tmp/opencode/test3.mjs` after the transit binding fix.
2. Debug timing minigame completion: confirm `#timing-hit` click invokes `timingHit()` three times, `timingGame.done` flips, `onComplete` fires, and `finishShift()` sets stage 1.
3. Verify hidden bus teleports to arena and sets stage 2.
4. Test full boss chain: barista → ferryman/hiker/mechanic (3 challengers → stage 4 storm) → raincoat → mirror → mayor → future → ending modal.
5. Verify all five ending availability conditions and `chooseEnding` flow.
6. Fix console warnings: remove `flatShading` from `MeshBasicMaterial` and replace `THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap` with `THREE.PCFShadowMap`.
7. Re-capture menu/play/phone/combat/ending screenshots; adjust lighting/arms if needed.
8. Commit all changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: orchestrator; all systems now appended, debug hooks at bottom.
- `src/data.js`: content definitions, bosses, quests, endings, events, styles.
- `src/world.js`: world geometry, lighting, weather, arena, interactables.
- `src/combat.js`: fight logic, boss AI, dodge/block additions.
- `src/npcs.js`: NPC models, schedules, nearest-NPC logic.
- `src/player.js`: movement, collision, driving, first-person arms.
- `src/ui.js`: HUD, panels, dialogue, modal, map, combat UI.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural rain/music/SFX.
- `index.html`: DOM IDs used by UI/main.

- `vendor/three.module.js`, `vendor/three.core.js`: local Three.js runtime.
- `fonts/`: local Bebas/Plex/Inter fonts.

- `/tmp/opencode/test4.mjs`: boot/start smoke test.

# BELLINGHAM: THE UNDERGROUND

An original, fully playable first-person open-world life sim and arcade fighting game set in a fictionalized Bellingham, Washington. Clock in, pay rent, fall in love, and try not to notice the city breathing back. Every stranger is a fighter. Every night is a round.

**18+.** Contains violence, crime, alcohol and drug themes, profanity, and psychological horror. Romance and intimacy are between consenting adults only, are non-graphic, and fade to black. There is no sexual violence or exploitation. All characters are adults. This is a work of fiction.

## Run it

No framework, no build step. The game is static HTML/CSS/JS with a locally vendored Three.js and local fonts.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8123
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:8123/>. A modern desktop or mobile browser with WebGL is required.

On the hosted runtime, `start.sh` serves the project automatically.

## Controls

### On foot (keyboard + mouse)

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `W A S D` | Move |
| Mouse | Look |
| `Shift` | Sprint |
| `Ctrl` | Crouch |
| `Space` | Jump |
| `E` | Interact / talk |
| `Tab` | Phone |
| `M` | Map |
| `Esc` | Pause / close |

### Fighting

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `LMB` / `J` | Punch |
| `RMB` / `K` | Kick |
| `Q` | Block (hold) |
| `Space` | Dodge |
| `E` | Grapple |
| `R` | Special |
| `F` | Environmental attack |
| `C` | Finisher (when the meter is ready) |

### Driving

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `W` / `S` | Throttle / brake-reverse |
| `A` / `D` | Steer |
| `F` | Exit the car |

### Touch

Phones and tablets get a virtual stick, a look area, and context buttons for interact, jump, phone, sprint, and the full fight set (punch, kick, block, dodge, special). Touch controls respect safe areas and disable page gestures over the game surface.

## What is in the game

- **A living city.** Downtown, Fairhaven, Boulevard Park, the waterfront, WWU, Whatcom Falls, Lake Whatcom, Chuckanut, the marina, industrial lots, trails, and Mount Baker on the horizon. Rain, fog, storms, wet streets, traffic, pedestrians, wildlife, and a day/night cycle.
- **A life sim.** Jobs and shifts, rent and home ownership, food and cooking, sleep, hygiene, mood, gym training, bars, cafés, clubs, dating, relationships, clothing, hair, tattoos, vehicles, skills, reputation ranks, quests, and saving/loading.
- **A fighting game.** Ten named bosses, each with their own style and AI. Punch, kick, block, dodge, counter, grapple, combo, specials, environmental attacks, stamina, health, special meters, slow-motion finishers, and learnable fighting styles.
- **A story that starts normal.** The first shift is just a shift. Then the transit board flickers, a bus takes a road that was always there, and the city begins to stutter. The underground tournament is only the first layer.
- **The ten names:** THE BARISTA, THE FERRYMAN, THE HIKER, THE MECHANIC, THE STUDENT, THE OLD MAN AT THE PARK, THE RAINCOAT, THE MAYOR, THE MIRROR, and THE FUTURE PLAYER.
- **Hundreds of encounters.** 24 authored random events plus 480 procedurally generated street encounters, scaled by how much the simulation is glitching.
- **Artifacts, secrets, and alternate realities.** The brass token, the raincoat button, the mirror shard, the cassette. The Quiet Table. The thin door into the version of Bellingham that watches this one.
- **Five endings.** Escape, become champion, shut it down, take control, or stay. Requirements are tracked in the phone's journal. You can also ignore the tournament and live normally for as long as you like.

## Project layout

```text
index.html          DOM shell, HUD, menus, touch controls
styles.css          all layout and visual styling
src/main.js         orchestrator: state, story, jobs, phone, endings, input
src/world.js        procedural city, weather, arena, interactables
src/player.js       first-person movement, collision, driving, arms
src/npcs.js         NPC models, schedules, memory, ambient crowds
src/combat.js       fight loop, boss AI, meters, effects
src/ui.js           HUD, panels, dialogue, modal, map, combat UI
src/audio.js        procedural Web Audio music, rain, and SFX
src/data.js         characters, bosses, items, quests, events, styles
vendor/             local Three.js runtime
fonts/              local display and text fonts
```

Saves use `localStorage` under `bellingham_underground_save_v3`. The pause menu can erase a save.

## Notes

- All characters, businesses, art, music, dialogue, and events are original.
- The city is a fictionalized version of Bellingham, not a map of the real place.
- Built with Three.js (MIT) and locally bundled fonts. See the font licenses in `fonts/` and the vendored Three.js license in `vendor/`.
